chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated from his paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who recites one hundred verses which he prays with at night, Allah will write for him, by them, the qunut of a night, and the one who recites two hundred verses at night in other than the night prayer, Allah will write for him in the Preserved Tablet a kantar of good deeds. A kantar is a thousand and two hundred okes, and one oke is greater than Mount Uhud.

key_terms.أُوقِيَّةٍ: Oke (a unit of weight), used to define the magnitude of the kantar
key_terms.اللَّوْحِ الْمَحْفُوظِ: Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz (The Preserved Tablet), the divine record where deeds are inscribed
key_terms.جَبَلِ أُحُدٍ: Mount Uhud, a famous mountain in Medina used here as a benchmark for great size or weight
key_terms.قُنُوتَ: Qunut (supplication/devotion), here referring to the spiritual status or reward of a night's devotion
key_terms.قِنْطَارًا: Kantar (a unit of weight/measure), used here metaphorically to denote a vast quantity of good deeds

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting two hundred verses of the Quran at night?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar*, this hadith highlights the Shia emphasis on the quantitative merit of Quranic recitation, distinguishing between the spiritual intercession of *qunut* during night prayer and the accumulation of pure good deeds (*hasanat*) outside of it. The metaphor of a 'kantar' (weighing over 400 ounces) exceeding Mount Uhud underscores the immense, tangible value of even modest recitation efforts in the divine ledger.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, from his paternal uncle, Muhammed bin Abi’l-Qasim, from Muhammed bin Isa, from Hasan bin Ali, from Ishaq bin Ammar, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

The one who recites a hundred verses which he prays with at a night, Allah will write for him, by them, the qunut [1] of a night, and the one who recites two hundred verses art a night in other than the night prayer, Allah will write for him in the Preserved Tablet a kantar of good deeds. A kantar [2] is a thousand and two hundred okes [3], and one oke is greater than Mount Uhud [4].
